messages:
Maya Chen: Quick heads-up — after the quantization sweep for halogen-lite (int8 per-channel), we see a persistent recall@10 drop on the short-query holdout (~4.1% absolute). Opening this thread to track possible propagation/drift.
Owen Patel: Ugh. Is that vs our baseline float32 or vs the previous quantized candidate?
Maya Chen: Vs float32 baseline on the same holdout (10k short queries). Float32 recall@10 = 0.782, int8 = 0.741.
Liam Garcia: Can you paste the eval summary and the sample failure cases?
Maya Chen: Pasted below — summary from eval-bot run:
```
EvalBot summary:
- dataset: short_query_holdout_10k
- baseline (float32): recall@1=0.56 recall@5=0.69 recall@10=0.782
- halogen-lite int8: recall@1=0.52 recall@5=0.66 recall@10=0.741
- avg cosine shift (pos-neg): 0.012 -> larger negative drift on short sequences
``` 
Maya Chen: Examples: small customer support queries, 3-6 words, nearest neighbor often replaced by near-synonym.
Jin Park: Do we have per-query-length breakdown? Might be concentrated on <=8 tokens.
Maya Chen: Yes — recall@10 drop concentrated on <=8 tokens: -6% relative. Longer queries unaffected.
Sophie Martinez: Could be embedding normalization interplay with quant scale. Did quant calibration use the same per-channel stats as for long seqs?
Owen Patel: IIRC we used global calibration window from the mixed-length training shard. That can bias small-seq activation distributions.
Liam Garcia: Quick experiment idea: rerun quant calibration using only short-query representative batch and recompute. If that recovers, it's calibration mismatch not model architecture.
Maya Chen: Agreed. Planning a quick A/B: (A) int8 recalibrated-on-short, (B) int8 original. Will run on staging 20k queries.
EvalBot: Scheduled eval jobs:
- job_id: ev-1717123499-A (recalibration-short)
- job_id: ev-1717123502-B (orig-calib)
- results ETA ~ 12m
Maya Chen: If A helps, we can bake new calibration profile into Dedicated bring-up and re-run rollout canary.
Owen Patel: Another angle — try L2 normalization before quant in the pipeline. That often stabilizes small vectors.
Jin Park: Add logging to capture top-3 nearest neighbor cosine distances pre/post so we can see margin compression.
Sophie Martinez: Also flag if nearest neighbor ID flips across quantization for seed queries. ID flips list will help triage.
EvalBot: ev-1717123499-A completed: recall@10=0.770 (recovery ~1.9%), ev-1717123502-B completed: recall@10=0.742
Maya Chen: Nice, recalibration recovered half the gap. Still ~1% behind float32.
Liam Garcia: For the remaining gap, try per-channel symmetric vs asymmetric quantization experiments, and run whitening (PCA) small-dim correction before quant.
Owen Patel: I can spin the asymmetric quant run on my nodepool, add per-channel stats + clip at 99.9th.
Maya Chen: Thanks. Also let's run clustering silhouette on short queries pre/post to see structural collapse.
Jin Park: I'll instrument the eval to output silhouette, mean intra-cluster distance, and ID-flip rate. Putting results in the thread when done.
Sophie Martinez: If per-channel asymmetric wins, we should add a conservative fallback: route short queries to float32 on Dedicated during rollout until quant variant verified.
Maya Chen: Agreed on fallback policy. I'll open rollout-config PR with canary rule: if recall@10 drop > 1% on short-query holdout, auto-fallback to float32 for requests < 10 tokens.
Liam Garcia: FYI I saw one weird failure where embedding vector norm crashed to 0.0001 after quant; adding guard to clip tiny norms.
Maya Chen: Good catch. Add guard + unit test. Thanks all — will update when asymmetric and clustering metrics land.
EvalBot: ev-1717123720 asymmetric-quant run queued.
Owen Patel: Ping me if you need help with the nodepool parallelism.
Maya Chen: Ending notes: triage steps so far: 1) calibrate-on-short (helped), 2) test asymmetric per-channel, 3) add L2-normalization option, 4) cluster/silhouette analysis, 5) decide canary fallback. Keeping ticket open.
Sophie Martinez: :thumbsup:
